## Vocabulary

Terms this pack was harvested with, grouped by their relation to the concept; counts are units matched / sources. Zero-hit terms are listed under Coverage. On every unit line, `keywords:` names the terms that matched.

- **self**: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification (13/4)

## Structure and components

- [statement] A Pub/Sub CDC update is not a full record snapshot: unchanged fields are present with empty values even when the stored record contains values. Determine changes from decoded changedFields and distinguish actual clearing from unchanged placeholders with nulledFields. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-deserialization-considerations.html · keywords: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-event-fields-body.html
- [statement] The community explanation of CDC states that events do not contain old values; the official body documentation describes updates using changed values and empty unchanged fields. Therefore, qualification of a particular old-to-new severity transition requires a previously maintained value or another explicit source of prior state; querying the current record after delivery does not recover the event’s old value. This state requirement is a design inference from the two sources. (medium confidence) — https://salesforce.stackexchange.com/questions/267759/trigger-oldmap-equivalent-in-changeevent · keywords: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-event-fields-body.html

## How it works

- [statement] For a specific old-to-new severity transition, maintain prior values in the consumer’s persistent store or consult field history when that field is tracked; querying the already committed record alone does not restore its previous values. This is a design inference from the documented payload and commit semantics. (medium confidence) — https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/decision-guides/guide/record-triggered · keywords: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification · also: https://salesforce.stackexchange.com/questions/267759/trigger-oldmap-equivalent-in-changeevent

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A channel-member filter can test entity fields and the event header’s change type, but cannot use the array-valued changedFields header. Filtered entity fields are automatically enriched. Consequently, a filter for a target severity value selects current matching state and can also deliver unrelated-field updates; the consumer still needs changedFields qualification to identify severity-field changes. This consequence is a design inference, not a documented transition-filter feature. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-filters.html · keywords: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-enrich-intro.html
- [statement] Multiple DML operations on the same record within one transaction produce one change event for the initial change type, carrying the final committed data. Salesforce illustrates a Case created at Medium priority and changed to High before commit: the result is one CREATE event with High priority. CDC cannot expose every intermediate severity transition inside that transaction. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-general-considerations.html · keywords: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Treat creation and undeletion qualification separately from update qualification: their Pub/Sub event bodies carry all record fields, and a newly created Case can already have High priority at commit. Decide explicitly whether those events should alert when the desired rule is a severity transition rather than initial high-severity state. (medium confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-event-fields-body.html · keywords: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-general-considerations.html
- [statement] Replayed enriched fields can contain their latest database values rather than their values when the event was stored, because enrichment is added at delivery. Fields that were actually changed in the event retain the correct changed values. Therefore, do not use an unchanged enriched severity field as historical proof of severity at the time of a replayed event. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-enrich-considerations.html · keywords: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification

## Facts and statements

- [statement] The Case object has an associated CaseChangeEvent object, introduced in API version 44.0. This provides the Case-specific CDC event object for lifecycle alert consumers. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/object-reference/references/standard-objects/object-case.html · keywords: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification
- [statement] Native CDC carries new field values and omits the prior record state. A transition that depends on a specific previous severity therefore needs additional prior-state evidence. (high confidence) — https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/decision-guides/guide/record-triggered · keywords: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification · also: https://salesforce.stackexchange.com/questions/267759/trigger-oldmap-equivalent-in-changeevent
- [statement] Pub/Sub CDC changedFields, diffFields, and nulledFields are bitmaps, not decoded field-name lists. Decode them against the event schema before testing whether the severity field changed. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-deserialization-considerations.html · keywords: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification
- [statement] CDC collapses multiple operations on the same record within one transaction into one event using the initial change type and final committed values. Salesforce’s example creates a Case, changes its priority from Medium to High before commit, and emits one CREATE event with High priority. An UPDATE-only severity rule therefore excludes this creation scenario and does not observe every internal priority step. (low confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-general-considerations.html · keywords: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification
- [statement] Joe Pugh’s 2020 engineering write-up independently reports that native Salesforce CDC delivers new field values without previous values; this historical observation agrees with the current Salesforce architecture guide. (high confidence) — https://mishimaltd.medium.com/event-driven-salesforce-change-data-capture-8308051841fc · keywords: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification · also: https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/decision-guides/guide/record-triggered
- [statement] Before qualifying a severity-field change in a Pub/Sub consumer, decode the changedFields and nulledFields bitmaps against the event schema; the schema can be obtained with GetSchema. Payload field presence alone does not establish a change. (high confidence) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/pub-sub-api/guide/event-deserialization-considerations.html · keywords: Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification · also: https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/platform/change-data-capture/guide/cdc-event-fields-body.html

## Research summary — Salesforce Case change events and severity-transition qualification

Case change events provide record-change input for alert qualification. Native CDC omits prior values, so a specific old-to-new severity transition needs retained state or suitable field history. Pub/Sub consumers must decode field-change bitmaps and distinguish unchanged empty values from fields actually nulled. Value filters and enrichment do not establish that severity changed. Transaction consolidation also means a Case created and reprioritized before commit can arrive as a creation with its final priority. The alert specification must define its severity field, target values, required prior state, and treatment of creation.
